      "title": "[Security] Desktop: any website can steal the OWNER-level agent API token — renderer serves CORS `*` and embeds the token in the index HTML",

      "repository": "elizaos/eliza",
      "body": "## Summary

The ElizaOS desktop app starts a local **renderer HTTP server** (Electrobun main process, `Bun.serve`, default `127.0.0.1:5174`, incrementing if taken). Two flaws on this server combine:

1. **Every static response is served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`** — JavaScript on any website can read the response bodies cross-origin.
2. **The built-in index page embeds the app's boot config in plaintext**, including the agent API's **OWNER-level Bearer token (`apiToken`)** and its base URL (`apiBase`).

So if the victim simply opens any attacker-controlled web page while the desktop app is running, that page performs one plain cross-origin GET (a simple request, **no preflight**) to `http://127.0.0.1:5174/`, reads the full HTML, and extracts the OWNER token with a regex. Zero interaction, no dialogs, completely silent — the app's highest-privilege credential is handed to an arbitrary website.

## Environment

- `@elizaos/app` 2.0.3-beta.7 (commit `876317fb`), Windows 11, default local configuration (no special settings)

## Root cause

`packages/app/platforms/electrobun/src/index.ts` — static-file handling of the renderer server:

```ts
// index.ts:915-933 — HTML branch
if (mimeExt === ".html" || filePath.endsWith("index.html")) {
    const html = apiBaseOwner.injectIntoHtml(content.toString("utf8"));  // :925 — injects apiToken + apiBase into the page
    return new Response(html, {
        headers: {
            "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
            "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",                           // :929 — any origin may read this
            "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=0, must-revalidate",
        },
    });
}
```

```ts
// index.ts:934-937 — all other static assets
const headers: Record = {
    "Content-Type": getRendererAssetContentType(mimeExt),
    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",                                   // :936
    ...
};
```

Either flaw alone would be harmless (no token embedded → nothing to steal; no `ACAO: *` → body unreadable cross-origin). Together, the OWNER credential leaves the victim's machine into the attacker's page context.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the desktop app (default config). The renderer listens on `127.0.0.1:5174`.
2. Open any other web page (any http/https origin — even `file://` works, which is convenient for verification) and run this from the browser console:

```js
const r = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:5174/", { cache: "no-store" });
const html = await r.text();
console.log(r.headers.get("access-control-allow-origin")); // "*"  (cross-origin read allowed)
console.log(html.match(/apiToken:"([0-9a-fA-F]+)"/)[1]);   // the OWNER-level Bearer token
console.log(html.match(/apiBase:"([^"]+)"/)[1]);           // e.g. http://127.0.0.1:31337
```

3. The console prints the OWNER token.

Self-contained attacker page (save as `.html`, open in a browser on the victim machine, click the button):

```html


attacker page


ElizaOS Desktop — cross-origin OWNER token theft PoC (this page is the "attacker website")


Renderer port (default 5174): 







```

## Expected / actual

- **Expected:** an external origin cannot read the local renderer's responses, and the OWNER token is never exposed to web content.
- **Actual:** `ACAO: *` lets any origin read the index HTML, which contains the OWNER Bearer token in plaintext.

## Impact (and honest scope)

- The agent API's **OWNER credential itself is exfiltrated** to any website the user visits — zero interaction beyond opening a page.
- Directly replaying **write** requests (POST/PUT) from the browser with the stolen token is rejected with 403: the agent API's loopback-trust check refuses requests carrying an untrusted `Origin` header (`packages/core/src/security/loopback-trust.ts:347-416`). The damage here is the credential leaving the machine, plus chaining with any local process or other issues — a local process holding this token can call the full API as OWNER.
- Chrome's Local Network Access (LNA), if enforced, would block page→127.0.0.1 requests; default Chrome/Firefox today are affected.
- Not applicable in external/cloud connection mode (no `apiToken` embedded there).

## Suggested fix

1. **Remove `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`** from static responses (`index.ts:929`, `index.ts:936`). The desktop UI does not need to be readable by arbitrary web origins.
2. **Don't embed the long-lived OWNER token in the HTML** (`injectIntoHtml`): deliver it via one-time runtime IPC, or use short-lived per-session credentials bound to the app's own processes.
3. If the UI must be served over HTTP, put an **Origin allowlist** on the renderer server (app protocol / loopback same-origin only).",

      "author": "lalalune",
      "number": 33368,
      "body": "# Relates to

Core mixed the runtime kernel with host configuration, domain DTOs, acoustic processing, assistant tests and application scripts. Private imports and forwarding modules obscured ownership and made independent cleanup difficult.

# Change

- Keep the Node runtime in `@elizaos/core` and portable kernel contracts in `@elizaos/core/protocol`. Internal modules import their defining files. JSON catalog assets keep explicit exports.
- Move HTTP, boot/configuration, registries, process policy and direct-media helpers to `@elizaos/host`; move domain DTOs, validation, LifeOps declarations and backup formats to `@elizaos/contracts`; move portable acoustic algorithms to `@elizaos/voice`. Core depends on none of those owners. Hosts explicitly compose assistant behavior, storage and providers.
- Migrate monorepo imports, mocks, dynamic types and build aliases together. Remove personal-assistant contract, app automation and UI domain/voice forwarding modules. Native-inference's existing optional local router remains an optional peer, avoiding a UI/provider dependency cycle.
- Fix conservative fact equality, immutable-image cache identity, deadline-factory rejection, awareness invalidation races, corrupt-registry errors and atomic registry publication. Preserve authorization, tenant isolation, cancellation, complete context, effect receipts and persisted backup bytes.
- Consolidate retry, scope predicates, migrations, mutation delegation, backup-reader cleanup, environment helpers and API-key hints. Keep model attempt/stream/failover settlement under its existing lifetime owner.
- Move assistant tests/live routing/latency tooling, identity merging and shared fixtures to their owners. Remove dead helpers, retired scripts, disabled APIs and redundant configuration. Exclude benchmark/generator sources from publication and verify installed tarballs.

Breaking import migration for the next release:

| Previous ownership | Public destination |
|---|---|
| Kernel implementation leaves | `@elizaos/core` or browser-safe `@elizaos/core/protocol` |
| Host configuration / HTTP / process helpers | `@elizaos/host` or browser-safe `@elizaos/host/protocol` |
| Domain and backup contracts | `@elizaos/contracts`; Node signing/verification uses `/node` |
| Portable acoustic processing | `@elizaos/voice` |
| Identity merge | `@elizaos/plugin-relationships` |
| Former `@elizaos/ui/types` forwarding entry | `@elizaos/contracts` |

These changes deliberately remove compatibility forwarding for retired imports. Voice algorithm bodies are unchanged after parsed-syntax comparison. Concurrent develop changes through `6084ff17cff4047e339fb01891b3c555c9a92fc2` are retained, including media cancellation, complete evaluator context and scoped SQLite reads.

# Testing

Pinned Bun 1.4.2 and Node 24.15.0. All task commits through 1d70383dbe60236f314b7a071a59e7f686c4bdd8 are merged into develop 6f2c1fa4e36483002f3521889dc515c8c1c7f95a through integration PR #33377. Local results below qualify this PR head; the larger combined integration has separate qualification.

Installed kernel verification covers host JSON loading, settings precedence, explicit composition, real provisioning, deterministic inference, redaction and supervision; installed production closure is 25 packages.
